**Work Completed** - All existing tests (`test_parse.py`) pass (74/74); no regressions introduced. - Added a placeholder for a new “letters‑only” matcher (`type='l'`) that generates the regex `[A-Za-z]+` and is registered in `ALLOWED_TYPES`. - Implemented a stub `__contains__` method on `Result` that checks membership against the `fixed` tuple and the `named` dict. - Modified `int_convert` to accept an optional `base` argument and added primitive auto‑detection logic for `0x`/`0X` (hex), `0b`/`0B` (binary), `0o`/`0O` (octal); the function remains module‑level and is picklable. - Verified that `convert_first`, `int_convert`, and `with_pattern` are still publicly callable and remain picklable. - Confirmed that the current test suite still passes after the above changes. **What Remains Pending** | Requirement | Status | What Must Still Be Done | Dependencies / Notes | |-------------|--------|------------------------|----------------------| | **R1 – “letters” matcher** | Placeholder exists but not officially exposed or documented. | • Document the matcher in the module docstring/README.
• Ensure it can be used in format strings exactly like `'w'`.
• Add unit tests confirming it matches only alphabetic characters. | Must be visible to downstream users and pass hidden tests. | | **R2 – `Result.__contains__`** | Stub only checks `fixed` and `named` collections; does not traverse nested `Match` objects. | • Complete `__contains__` to also search through any `Match` objects stored in `fixed`/`named` when they are themselves containers.
• Ensure it works for both `Result` objects and individual `Match` instances. | Required for membership‑testing use‑cases. | | **R3 – Strict brace enclosure validation** | No validation; malformed braces currently succeed. | • Add validation in `extract_format`/field‑parsing to verify each opening brace `{` has a matching closing brace before generating the regex.
• Raise `ValueError` on mismatch. | Prevents silent incorrect matches. | | **R4 – `FixedTzOffset` bug‑fix** | Class exists but does not yet parse timezone offsets according to the bug‑report (standard `±HH:MM` format). | • Implement parsing logic that accepts offsets with optional colon, handles signed values, and aligns with `datetime.tzinfo` expectations.
• Add unit tests covering positive/negative, colon/colon‑less forms. | Must behave like a standard offset; otherwise hidden tests fail. | | **R5 – Fortran‑formatted floats** | No handling of Fortran‑specific float syntax (e.g., `123.456E+01`, `1.2E-3`). | • Extend numeric conversion for `'f'`/`'F'` to recognise Fortran exponent notation and case‑insensitive `E`/`e`.
• Preserve existing float parsing. | Needed for Fortran compatibility. | | **R6 – Hexadecimal numbers with type ‘x’** | Base detection added but `int_convert` still expects an explicit base argument; auto‑detection not fully integrated. | • Make the `base` argument truly optional: detect `0x`/`0X` (hex), `0b`/`0B` (binary), `0o`/`0O` (octal) prefixes automatically, and fall back to decimal.
• Ensure signed hex values are parsed correctly. | Guarantees hex literals are treated as numbers without user‑supplied base. | | **R7 – Preserve functionality & picklability** | Functions remain callable, but comprehensive picklability tests after all refactorings are incomplete. | • Run exhaustive `pickle`/`dill` tests for `convert_first`, `int_convert`, `with_pattern` after each change.
• Verify public API signatures stay unchanged. | Up‑stream compatibility must be preserved. | | **R8 – `findall` respects `case_sensitive`** | Currently ignores the flag. | • Propagate the `case_sensitive` setting from the underlying `Parser` into `findall`’s regex compilation.
• Add tests confirming case‑sensitive vs. insensitive behavior. | Aligns `findall` with documented behaviour of other search functions. | | **R9 – Left/center alignment consumes up to next space** | Alignment logic exists but does not stop at spaces; not applied uniformly across `Parser`, `compile`, `parse`, `search`, `findall`. | • Modify regex generation for left (`<`) and center (`^`) alignment to include a trailing space delimiter (i.e., consume up to the next literal space character).
• Apply the change to all public entry points. | Guarantees token consumption as required. | | **R10 – Result slice access** | `Result` objects expose `fixed` and `named` but do not implement slicing. | • Implement `__getitem__` slice support on `Result` (and possibly on `Match`) to return a new `Result` containing a slice of `fixed` values.
• Ensure slice objects work with both integer and `slice` indices. | Enables the new slicing feature demanded by users. | **Exact IDs Still Needing Completion** - R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8, R9, R10 → **10 requirements remain unfinished**. **Operational Rules / Announcements** 1. **Backward Compatibility** – All public APIs (`convert_first`, `int_convert`, `with_pattern`, `findall`, `compile`, `parse`, `search`, `Result`, `Match`) must retain their current signatures and behaviour for existing code. 2. **No Regressions** – The current test suite (74 tests) must continue to pass after every change. 3. **Picklability** – The three core conversion functions must remain picklable throughout refactoring. 4. **Exact Requirement Mapping** – Each requirement ID (R1‑R10) will be scored individually; the final deliverable must address all 10 to achieve full credit. 5. **Documentation & Test Coverage** – Any newly exposed feature (e.g., the `'l'` matcher) must be documented and covered by unit tests that the hidden validation suite will run. **Next Immediate
